The true event-trigger denominator is not available yet

The figures above use unique recipients of the comm #1 email as a proxy for journey entries, on the basis of the 26 Aug finding that 100% of triggering buyers received an email. The real denominator is distinct users firing chatMessageCreated where receiver != 'professional'.

A Hex thread run against the warehouse on 13 Sep could not produce it: there is no accessible Iterable custom-event table carrying chatMessageCreated, its receiver field, user ID and event timestamp together, and the current connection was denied query access to the curated email_log_iterable / push_log_iterable / sms_log_iterable tables. Until data eng exposes the event stream, every trigger-based percentage on this page is a proxy, not a measurement.

Do not report the current SMS click rate as a win

Iterable are checking whether bot-filtering rules regressed on this campaign: every SMS click event carries an isBot flag, and the filtered figure excludes flagged clicks. They have seen a batch of clearly automated clicks stop being flagged before, and have confirmed the quiet-hours removal could not move click rate this far. Treat 8 Sep onwards as suspect until they come back.

What we need to fill this table

  • Query access to insight_roots.email_log_iterable, push_log_iterable and sms_log_iterable for the Hex connection.
  • An exposed Iterable custom-event source with chatMessageCreated, receiver, user ID and UTC timestamp.
  • A point-in-time buyer SMS consent field. buyer_notify_email_eligible is email eligibility and must not be used as SMS consent.
  • Point-in-time app-install / push-enabled state. buyer_has_app is lifetime ("has logged in at least once"), so it overstates eligibility for push and understates it for SMS.

Worth adding to Ailish's IST-6640 rather than raising separately.

Test results summary

Click rate declined against control, and in the transactional cell that decline was large enough to be statistically significant. Open rate was flat.

Downstream, the test moved the other way: more buyers returned to site within 24 hours, more returned via the app, and in the marketing cell more went on to respond to the professional. The one downstream metric that softened was responses in the transactional cell.

Fewer clicks but no loss of returns or responses points at the CTA change rather than at engagement: control offered two buttons plus an inline inbox link, so it collected extra low-intent clicks that were never going to convert. On that basis the new design was shipped to 100% on 2 Sep — the decision rested on what buyers did after the click, not on the click itself.
